title: Tele2: RCS on iPhone and Android
finding: Tele2 states on its support page that RCS can be used on iPhone and Android when the right conditions are met.
implication: The statement covers the operator's description of private chat. Check your own subscription and business reach separately.

title: Comviq: RCS on iPhone and Android
finding: Comviq describes RCS on iPhone and Android on its support page.
implication: Go by Comviq's answer for your number, not only by which network the operator uses.

title: Apple: Carrier support in Europe
finding: Apple publishes carrier features by country and carrier in its European support list.
implication: Read the right country section and compare it with the carrier's own information. A list entry does not settle business reach.

title: Apple: iMessage, RCS and SMS/MMS
finding: Apple's Messages can use iMessage, RCS and SMS/MMS. RCS and SMS can both appear with green bubbles.
implication: The bubble color does not tell RCS from SMS; the channel text in the conversation gives better information.

title: Google RCS for Business: Receive messages
finding: Google documents incoming customer messages, including text and media content.
implication: Receive and assess the customer's actual reply; a button-driven dialog also needs to handle other content.

title: Google RCS for Business: Launch details
finding: Google has separate launch details and launch status for business agents.
implication: A test agent that has been created is not the same as a sender approved for public sends.

title: Google RCS for Business: Analytics
finding: Google has separate documentation for measurement in RCS for Business.
implication: Read the definitions behind the report. Channel statistics and purchase data come from different sources and need to be linked for business analysis.

title: IMY: The right to object
finding: IMY states that the data subject can always object to the processing of personal data for direct marketing.
implication: An objection must take effect in the sending systems. This right alone does not answer questions about retention periods or other legal bases.

title: Konsumentverket: The Marketing Act
finding: Konsumentverket describes requirements including identification of advertising and that marketing must not be misleading.
implication: A new message format does not change the requirements for a clear sender or for evidence of claimed customer results.

title: GSMA: RCS Universal Profile
finding: Universal Profile is GSMA's common technical foundation for RCS.
implication: A common standard does not mean that every carrier or app has introduced the same features.

title: Google Messages: Common questions about RCS chats
finding: Google Messages uses Wi-Fi or mobile data for RCS and shows the connection status in the app.
implication: Check both the connection and the channel in the conversation in question; having the setting turned on is not enough.

title: Google Messages: RCS chats with businesses
finding: Google describes business RCS separately from private chats, with a business profile and the option to block the sender.
implication: Private RCS support should not be used as proof that a given business sender reaches the customer.

title: Apple: About RCS messages on iPhone
finding: Apple lists iOS 18 or later and a carrier with RCS support as requirements on iPhone.
implication: The system version alone gives no reliable answer about support on a Swedish subscription or for business sends.

title: Google Messages: How RCS chats protect your conversations
finding: Google describes end-to-end encryption for eligible private RCS conversations in Google Messages.
implication: That protection should not be assumed for business RCS. Sender verification and encryption are different things.

title: Google RCS for Business: Create an agent
finding: In Google's business model, the sender is represented by an agent with brand and contact details.
implication: The agent is a registered sender, not automatically a chatbot or AI. The customer's systems control what it does.

title: Google RCS for Business: Brand verification
finding: Google's brand verification checks the brand and the partner's authorization before launch.
implication: An approved identity is neither a quality certificate for the offer nor permission to contact every recipient.

title: Google RCS for Business: Rich cards
finding: Google documents rich cards with media, title, description and suggestions, as well as carousels of cards.
implication: Choose the format based on the content and test it on recipient devices. A richer format does not by itself give a better result.

title: Google RCS for Business: What can agents do?
finding: Google distinguishes suggested replies from actions such as opening a web address.
implication: A sent reply and a visit to a website are different events. A completed booking must be confirmed in the booking system.

title: Google RCS for Business: Send messages
finding: Google documents sending, error handling and limitations for its RCS for Business service.
implication: Use the documentation for your actual provider. That a request was accepted is not a delivery confirmation.

title: Google RCS for Business: Receive events
finding: Google distinguishes the delivery event DELIVERED from the read event READ for business messages.
implication: The statuses describe different steps. Neither delivery nor reading proves understanding, consent or a purchase.

title: Google RCS for Business: Webhooks
finding: Google's business RCS sends incoming messages and events to a configured webhook.
implication: The receiver needs to verify requests and handle redeliveries without changing the same customer case more than once.

title: Google RCS for Business: Capability checks
finding: Google's capability check examines reach and supported features for a phone number and a business agent.
implication: It is more specific than phone model or carrier name, but it is not a receipt for a later send.

title: Google RCS for Business: Best practices
finding: Google recommends relevant messages, clear user choices and respect for the recipient's wishes.
implication: This is guidance, not a measured campaign result. The effect needs to be followed in your own customer journey.

title: Bandwidth: Updates to RCS for Business agent logos in Google Messages
finding: Bandwidth writes that Google Messages shows logos for RCS businesses as rounded squares instead of circles, that verified senders get a checkmark after the name, and that the logo should be 224 × 224 px with a solid background. All logos must be updated by June 1, 2027.
implication: The information comes from a provider's customer notice about Google's change, not from a measurement. Check the requirements with your partner before changing the logo.
